arabic.text: تَعْرُجُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ إِلَيْهِ فِى يَوْمٍۢ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُۥ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍۢ (٤)

keywords.def: stopping on a word, with a breath
a madd before a sukoon made by stopping
ة, read as haa at a stop
an echo on ق ط ب ج د

questions.q: Stop on «ٱلْمَعَارِجِ» (70:3) and describe what happens.
questions.a: The kasrah drops, the ج takes a sukoon and a clear qalqalah: al-ma'aarij.

questions.q: Taa marbutah at a stop becomes ...
Ending drill (pupil PDF): write how you stop on the last word of each ayah in 70:12 to 22. Today's rota group recites 70:12 to 22.
questions.a: وَأَخِيهِ: akheeh; تُـْٔوِيهِ: tu'weeh; يُنجِيهِ: yunjeeh; لَظَىٰ: lazaa; لِّلشَّوَىٰ: lish-shawaa; وَتَوَلَّىٰ: wa tawallaa; فَأَوْعَىٰٓ: fa'aw'aa; هَلُوعًا: haloo'aa; جَزُوعًۭا: jazoo'aa; مَنُوعًا: manoo'aa; ٱلْمُصَلِّينَ: al-musalleen ('arid).

questions.q: Extend: choose a breath point in 70:4 and justify it.
questions.a: After «إِلَيْهِ» (the angels ascend to Him), then restart at «فِى يَوْمٍ»: the meaning stays sound.

questions.q: Stretch: why is stopping in the middle of 70:4 still not ideal?
questions.a: It is one connected sentence; an ayah end is the best stop.
A) waaqi'. Tanween kasrah is dropped at a stop: waaqi'.

questions.q: Think again: When you stop on a word, it changes a little. Why do you think Arabic allows the ending to change at a stop?
questions.a: Arabic never stops on a moving vowel; a stop makes the last letter quiet, which is easier and clearer.
